attributes.probed_form:
KEEP (commit 92d8d6654, fuzzy 88.6120 -> 88.8095, real 1180 -> 1177, insns 1023 -> 1020, multiset 26t -> 23t). Inside `if (uv2Ptr != 0)`, the carrier declaration `u16 v2 = pbSwap16(*(u16*)uv2Ptr);` became `u32 v2 = pbSwap16(*(u16*)uv2Ptr);`. ONE character class, three instructions. Mechanism, read from the aligned view at +0x9ac before the edit: the three following statements are `uv2[0] = (f32)((v2 & 0x1F) << 3);`, `uv2[1] = (f32)((v2 >> 2) & 0xF8);` and `uv2[2] = (f32)((v2 >> 7) & 0xF8);`. With a u16 carrier each masked expression has type `int` after integral promotion, so MWCC selects the SIGNED int-to-double magic and emits `xoris rX,rX,32768` before each `stw`, then subtracts the signed bias constant. The target emits no xoris at any of the three and subtracts a DIFFERENT FPR constant - i.e. it used the unsigned magic - which is only reachable if the expression type is unsigned. Widening the carrier to u32 makes all three expressions unsigned and reproduces the target's form and its bias constant. The values are 8-bit masked quantities, so the change is provably semantics-preserving.

NEGATIVE, reverted, and a WARNING about trusting real and count distance together. `kick = ((nv >> 15) & 1) != 0;` became `kick = (nv >> 15) & 1;` on the reasoning that the `!= 0` is redundant on an already-0/1 value and that ours carried a surplus `clrlwi r0,r0,24` before the byte store. It measured real 1177 -> 1143 (-34) AND count distance 7 -> 3 - two large gains in the two cheapest predictors - while multiset went 23t -> 25t and fuzzy 88.8095 -> 88.7068. The aligned read settled it: the edit DELETED an `addic`/`subfe`/`clrlwi` triple that the TARGET CONTAINS. The `!= 0` is the correct source form; the target really does normalise through the addic/subfe idiom. The real and count gains were pure alignment luck on a 1020-instruction function. Reverted, and the tree re-measured back to real 1177 / 1020 / 23t.

CORRECTION TO THE RUN-27 RECORD'S OWN UNTRIED LEAD, so the next lane does not spend the same reading: that record names 'the byte round-trip block at 0x4d4-0x568 approached from the pbSwap32 macro rather than from its argument' as the untried direction. Read at the aligned view this pass, the round-trip blocks are COUNT-EQUAL on both sides (4 lbz + 4 stb each); they differ only in that MWCC software-pipelines ours across two registers while the target uses one strictly alternating lbz/stb chain. There is no instruction to win there - it is schedule, not structure - so the lead as written is worth at most a schedule probe, not the structural rewrite its phrasing implies.
